transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time. I just came in because... I've been having a bit of a hard time lately, I guess. 

I keep catching myself thinking that... well, that maybe it might just be easier if I didn't wake up. It's silly, I know. And I want to be really clear, I haven't made any sort of plan to hurt myself or anything like that! I promise I haven't. I just... the thoughts kind of sneak up on me, and I figured I should probably talk to someone about it before it got worse. That's the right thing to do, isn't it?
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?

Um... well, it's been a little while. Nothing too drastic, I promise! Just... this low spell has kind of been hanging on for about three months now. Ever since I had a bit of a... a crash, I guess you could say. 

I probably should have come in sooner, I just didn't want to make a fuss if I could just shake it off on my own, you know? I hope it's okay that I waited. Does three months sound about normal for this kind of thing?
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in activities that you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I try to keep busy, I really do. But... yeah, lately, the things that usually settle me down just haven't been doing the trick. 

Usually, I love getting out to go fishing, or... or spending a Saturday digging through old vinyl records at the shop. I even used to really get a kick out of tailgating before the games, or just tinkering with my home-brew setup in the garage. But for the last little while, it's just... I don't know, it all just feels like a chore. Like I have to force myself to even care about it. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit lazy of me. I really am trying to snap out of it. Is it normal to just lose your spark for hobbies like that?
Have you experienced a decrease in pleasure from activities that you usually find enjoyable?

Um, well, I think that's pretty much what I was just trying to say, actually. About the fishing and the records and all that? I just... I don't get that same good feeling from them right now. 

I really hope I'm explaining this right. It's not that I hate doing those things now, it's just that the fun part seems to be missing lately. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. Am I making sense?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? Nothing to worry about, I promise! But, yeah, I suppose my jeans have been feeling a little looser lately. 

It's just... I don't know, most days I kind of have to remind myself to eat. I'll make supper, but then it just sits there on the plate and it feels like... like too much trouble to actually eat it. I'm sure my appetite will come back soon, though. I'm trying to be better about it, I really am. 

Is it okay that I haven't been eating as much? I know I should probably be taking better care of myself right now.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and fidgety?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I've noticed anything like that. I mean, I try to keep a good, steady pace, especially when I'm working the sales floor, you know? I haven't been dragging my feet, and I don't think I've been overly jittery or pacing around, either. I just try to keep things normal. 

I hope that's okay? I know I'm probably not giving you a lot to go on with that one, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. Is it alright if I haven't really had any trouble with that?
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Guilty? Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I always try to do my best by people, you know? At work and just... in general. I haven't done anything bad that I need to feel guilty about. 

I mean, I know I'm not perfect, and I feel a little bad about not eating right or keeping up with my hobbies like we talked about, but... not like a deep, terrible guilt or anything like that. I really try to be a good person. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're asking.
How often do you find yourself tearful or on the verge of tears lately?

Tearful? Oh, no, not really. I mean, I might get a little misty-eyed during a sad commercial or something, but... no, I haven't been crying or anything like that. I try to keep a positive attitude, you know? 

I don't want to be a bother to anyone or bring people down, so I just try to keep a smile on my face. I'm doing okay, really. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you been experiencing a lack of energy or feeling fatigued most of the time?

Energy? Oh, um... I think my energy is pretty good, actually. I mean, sure, working retail, you're on your feet all day, so my legs might get a little heavy after a long shift, but... no, I wouldn't say I'm fatigued or lacking energy most of the time. 

I always make sure I push through and get my work done. I don't want to be a burden to my manager or, you know, slack off on the floor. So I just keep moving and do what needs to be done. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I'm really trying to give you the right information, so just let me know if I'm doing this right.
Would you say your low mood and loss of interest in activities are present most of the day?

Oh, no, definitely not most of the day. I mean, everyone has a quiet moment here or there, right? But I really try to stay upbeat. At the store, you have to keep a good attitude for the customers, so I just focus on that and do my job. 

As for my activities... well, maybe I don't do quite as much as I used to when I get home, mostly just because I'm resting my feet, but I wouldn't call it a loss of interest. I'm not just sitting around feeling sad, I promise. I always try to look on the bright side and keep going. Is that... does that help explain it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.
How many days a week would you say you're experiencing this low mood?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it... maybe a few days a week? But it's not like a deep, terrible sadness, I promise. It's just... 

Well, a little while ago, I had this... this period where I had so much energy, you know? Just going and going. And then... after that burst of energy wore off, it kind of felt like somebody had just pulled the plug on me. I'd sit at the kitchen table in the mornings, just... staring at my coffee, feeling kind of empty. And honestly, a little ashamed that I couldn't just snap out of it and be productive. 

But I really try not to let it get to me, and I always make it to work. I don't let it ruin my whole week or anything. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.
For how many weeks have you been experiencing this low mood a few days a week?

Well, um... I suppose it's been a little while now. Maybe... about three months? Ever since that big crash I mentioned, when all that energy just sort of vanished. 

But really, it's just a little low spell, you know? It's been hanging on for those three months, but I'm managing it. I'm still getting out of bed, still putting on a smile for the customers. I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it for months on end. I'm really trying my best to push through it. Is three months... is that a normal amount of time for something like this? I hope I'm giving you the right details.
Would you say that your low mood is interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Well, I... I wouldn't say it's interfering *too* much. I mean, I still go to work, like I said! I'm trying really hard to keep up appearances there. 

But, um... at home, things have gotten a little... messy. I guess my routines have gotten a bit sloppy, to be honest. It's embarrassing to admit, but I've fallen behind on some bills. And I had a few days where I missed some important callbacks and appointments. I just... I couldn't seem to muster the energy, even though I knew I needed to. 

I even tried to look for a better paying job a little while back, because I really need the work, but I just couldn't keep a steady search going. I thought I could just push through it with willpower, but... I guess it got a little out of hand. I'm really trying to get back on track, though! I don't want you to think I'm just letting everything fall apart. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm not sounding too irresponsible.
Would you say that your low mood is significantly impacting your daily functioning, such as causing problems with work, relationships, or self-care?

Well, um... I guess I sort of just touched on that, didn't I? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much. But, yeah... I suppose it is impacting things a little more than I'd like to admit. 

Like I said, I'm still showing up for my shifts at the store, so work isn't a total disaster! But... yeah, at home, my usual routines have just gotten so sloppy. It's really not like me. I fell behind on those bills, and missing those callbacks and appointments... it just makes me feel so guilty. And the job search, too. I know I need the work, but I just couldn't keep it going steadily. 

I really thought I could just handle it by willpower, you know? Just buckle down and fix it. But I guess it got to the point where I realized I couldn't do it all on my own. I hope you don't think less of me for letting things slip like that. I'm really trying my best to be responsible. Am I giving you the right kind of information for your notes?
Would you say that your low mood is worse in the morning or does it stay fairly consistent throughout the day?

Oh, um... you know, I haven't really noticed a difference, to be honest. I guess it just stays fairly consistent? It's just sort of... lingering there in the background throughout the day. 

I try so hard to just keep busy and put on a good face from the minute my alarm goes off, so maybe I'm just not paying close enough attention to the exact timing of it all. 

I'm sorry if that's not a very helpful answer! I hope it's okay that I don't have a specific time of day to give you. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can without making a bigger deal out of it than it is. Does that... does that make sense for your notes?
Would you say that your low mood is significantly interfering with your daily life most days?

Well, I... I know we keep circling back to this, and I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record or... or like I'm making excuses. But, yes, I suppose it is interfering most days. 

I mean, like I mentioned before, it's just... the home stuff. The routines getting so sloppy. I really am usually much more on top of things! But... I did fall behind on those bills, and missing those appointments and callbacks... it's just not how I like to handle my responsibilities. And the job search... I really do need the work, but I just couldn't keep a steady search going. 

I kept telling myself I could just push through it, you know? Just use willpower to get everything back in order. But it got to the point where I realized I couldn't just fix it all by myself. I really am trying, though! I hope that's clear. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up on everything. Is that... is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm answering you properly.
Would you say that your low mood is causing significant distress or impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning?

Well, um... I know we've kind of gone over this a few times now, and I really hope I'm not being frustrating by repeating myself. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But, yes, I suppose it is causing some impairment. Like I was saying, it's mostly the stuff at home. I just got so behind on my bills, and I missed those important callbacks and appointments... which really isn't like me at all. I usually try to be so responsible. And with the job search... I really need the extra work, but I just couldn't keep it going steadily. 

My routines just got so sloppy that I finally had to admit to myself that my willpower wasn't enough to fix it this time. I hope you understand that I really was trying my best to keep it all together. I don't want to sound like I'm just letting my life fall apart. Does that answer your question okay? I want to be as helpful as possible for your evaluation.
Would you describe your current low mood as mildly bothersome or significantly debilitating?

Oh, gosh, um... I feel terrible because I know I keep giving you the exact same examples, and I really hope I'm not doing this wrong or misunderstanding you! 

I'd probably lean more toward mildly bothersome, to be completely honest. "Debilitating" just sounds so extreme, you know? I really don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is, because I know there are people out there dealing with much harder things. 

Like I was just mentioning, it's really just that my usual routines at home got a bit too sloppy for me to handle just by using my own willpower. Just the falling behind on the bills, missing those few callbacks and appointments, and not keeping up a steady job search even though I do need the work. It's frustrating, but I wouldn't call it debilitating. 

I really hope that's the right kind of answer for you. Am I understanding your question right, or did you need me to talk about a different part of my day? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes.
For how many days in a row have you been experiencing this low mood at its worst?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. I really hope I'm not making it sound like I've just been sitting around doing nothing all this time, because I have been trying to push through it. 

But, honestly, this low spell has been hanging on for about three months now... ever since that crash I mentioned. I know three months sounds like a long time to let things slide, and I feel a bit embarrassed admitting it's been going on that long. I really thought I could snap out of it sooner. 

Is that the kind of timeline you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details so you can figure out what's going on with me.

Would you say that your low mood is significantly interfering with your ability to function in daily life, such as impacting your work, relationships, or personal care, for most of the day, nearly every day?

Well, um... I feel like I'm just repeating myself again, and I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you new information. I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

I wouldn't say it's interfering with *everything* for most of the day, every day. That sounds a little too intense. It's really just the things I mentioned before... falling behind on my bills, missing a few callbacks and appointments, and not keeping up with my job search like I should, even though I really do need the extra work. 

It's just that my usual routines at home got a bit sloppy, and I finally realized I couldn't just fix it with willpower alone. I'm really trying my best, though, I promise. I don't want you to think I've completely given up or anything. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for.
